name: Nested NesGen: NES -> Genesis / Mega Drive
cli: brokendev.ps1 nested-everything nes2md <in.nes> <out.md> [-Profile <game id or file>] [-Feedback none|brokennes] [-Set key=value,...]
description: Static 6502 -> 68000 translation (recursive descent from the vectors, every instruction labelled, a 32 K dispatch table for RTS/RTI/JMP (ind)) linked with a 68000 runtime: the NMI runs from the VInt, PPU writes go to plane A (H32, top 8 lines cropped), attributes to palette bits, $3F00 to CRAM, $4014 to the sprite table, the pad to $4016, the 2A03 to the PSG. NROM with CHR-ROM only (the CHR is converted once at build time). The dynamic fallback is a dispatch miss: the ROM stops with the 6502 address in RAM ($FF8040) and -Feedback brokennes adds it as an entry and translates again.

settings.what: Measurement build: count every 6502 instruction run ($FF8018 total, $FF8034 inside NMIs). Slower; for the cost numbers only
fm: pulses and triangle on YM2612 channels 1-3 (duty as the modulator ratio/depth, triangle as a sine), noise on the PSG; psg: everything on the PSG (50% squares)
Lines added to the sprite-0 hit line (the hit reads set from OAM Y + 1 - 8 + spr0lag to the end of the picture)
Measurement build: count each 6502 opcode run inside NMIs (256 longs at $FF8400)

pads: NES A = Genesis C, B = B, Select = A, Start = Start
limits: mapper 0 with CHR-ROM only; no CHR-RAM, no banking
vertical mirroring: one 64x32 plane (horizontal nametable scrolling); horizontal mirroring: one 32x64 plane (the 240-line nametable height is not modelled, rows 30-31 show between the halves)
mid-frame splits only through $2005 writes (the scroll register takes effect on the next line); $2006 mid-frame scroll is not modelled
sprite 0 hit is timed from the V counter and sprite 0's Y, not from pixels; it reads clear in vblank
sweep and DMC are not reproduced; pulse duty is an FM timbre, not a real pulse width
a changed return address with an unchanged S is not caught by the native RTS
profiles: BrokenDev/projects/nested-nes2md/profiles/<game id>.json: entries ["C123", ...] (extra 6502 entry points; written by feedback)
